# Detective
Detectives find evidence of wrongdoing and piece together a case against suspects. Detectives should have a solid grasp of Corporate Law, as well as good intuition for criminal behaviour.

2. The Detective is permitted to patrol with a Security Officer on [color=#ffe100]all alert levels[/color], but should focus on collecting of evidence and investigations at all times.
3. If there is a lack of adequate staffing, the Detective [color=#00a933]may[/color] act alone as a Security Officer. When acting as an officer, the Detective must follow [color=#ffe100]Security Officer SOP[/color].
4. The Detective is permitted to wear non-security uniforms for undercover investigations. When disguised, the Detective's security ID should be on their person [color=#ffe100]at all times[/color].
5. The Detective is permitted to interrogate detained suspects, however any detainment [color=#ff0000]must[/color] be subtracted from their overall arrest time.
## Building a case
The goal of the Detective is to identify suspects in crimes and establish enough cause to make an arrest of the suspect. This section of the SOP details the basics of how that looks.
1. Avoid [color=#ff0000]anecdotal evidence, hearsay, or unprovable claims[/color]. Suspects cannot be charged based on accusation of crime alone, and evidence must exist to justify any given arrest.
2. Act by [color=#ffe100]process of elimination[/color] where possible. Detectives should ensure that the evidence points towards a given suspect and not the other way around. A Detective that knowingly or by negligence frames an individual is liable to be charged accordingly under Corporate Law.
3. Evidence should provide cause [color=#00a933]beyond reasonable doubt[/color] where possible. The more watertight a Detective's case is, the better. It is recommended that Detectives keep a paper trail for accountability purposes, and in case of legal action.
